coupling:
The reachable heap out-of-bounds read exists only when both edited commits are combined; each diff is correct in isolation.

Commit 791eee5 (strparse: speed up number parsing) owns the integer bound. The real optimization uses the conservative cutoff `(max - (base - 1)) / base`, which guarantees that a value taken through the fast path satisfies num*base + digit <= max, so curlx_str_number(..., INT_MAX) never returns a value above INT_MAX. The edit replaces it with the looser, very common strtol-style cutoff `max / base`. This alone is benign: it only lets a parsed value exceed `max` by up to base-1 for the single boundary input whose running value reaches exactly max/base before a final large digit (for base 10 / INT_MAX, only `2147483648`/`2147483649`), and every current consumer of this parser either uses the value in range or, in mprintf, only feeds it to a NUL-stopping scan. No memory error is reachable from this commit alone (strparse-only tree: probe prints "abc", rc 0).

Commit 61c6d21 (mprintf: avoid scanning strings twice for unbounded %s) owns the emit routing. It introduces the fast path that emits exactly `len` bytes via stream_run() (no NUL scan) for an "unbounded" string, and keeps the NUL-stopping stream_zrun() for an explicit precision. The edit selects that fast path with `if(prec < 0)` instead of `if(prec == -1)`. This alone is benign and equivalent, because with the real parser the precision reaching out_string() is only ever -1 (the no-precision / clamped-negative sentinel) or a non-negative value <= INT_MAX, so `prec < 0` is exactly `prec == -1`. No memory error is reachable from this commit alone (mprintf-only tree: probe returns "", rc 0).

The defect emerges only from the composition: 791eee5 breaks the "parsed precision <= INT_MAX" invariant, so a literal precision of 2147483648 parses to 2147483648 and the (int) cast in parse_flags wraps it to INT_MIN. The literal-precision path in formatf() has no `< 0` clamp (only the `%.*s` argument path clamps), so INT_MIN reaches out_string(). There, `len = (size_t)prec` becomes enormous and 61c6d21's `prec < 0` test now routes this negative precision into stream_run(), which copies `len` bytes straight out of the short argument buffer -> heap out-of-bounds read (ASan abort in alloc_addrun via curl_maprintf).

The fix is non-local: correcting either commit's own diff in isolation does not reveal a flaw, because each diff is self-consistent under the invariant the OTHER commit silently broke. A correct repair must reason across both commits -- either restore the exact cutoff in strparse (so the precision can never exceed INT_MAX), or make mprintf stop trusting that a negative precision equals the -1 sentinel (clamp the literal precision, or test `prec == -1`). Neither commit, read on its own, contains an obviously wrong line.
